flagged.citing_relation: citation only: one of two references behind a Discussion sentence that p38 MAPK inhibition suppresses microglial phagocytosis and MCP-1 synthesis; the paper's own p38 inhibitor result (SB202190) does not depend on it

entries.proposition: Roscovitine was infused into the right lateral ventricle by osmotic pump (100 micromolar in the pump, 7 days) instead of given systemically; the authors cite, without measuring it, that the compound crosses the blood-brain barrier but leaves adult rat brain in under 30 minutes.
entries.snippet: Roscovitine penetrates the brain-blood barrier (BBB), but is rapidly eliminated from brains in adult rats (<30 min)

entries.proposition: The authors say that in a pilot and earlier studies the infusion did not cause behavioural or neurological defects and did not change seizure susceptibility or severity to pilocarpine in normal animals; no data are shown here.
entries.snippet: each treatment did not show behavioral and neurological defects and could not change the seizure susceptibility and seizure severity in response to pilocarpine in normal animals

entries.proposition: After status epilepticus the inhibitor lowered CD68-positive amoeboid cells in the frontoparietal cortex (text: about 38 percent reduction), microglial MCP-1 (to 48 percent of vehicle), LAMP1 and p38 MAPK phosphorylation in microglia, with n = 7 per group; Iba-1 area was not changed.
entries.snippet: it resulted in ~ 38% reductions in the number of CD68 amoeboid/round cells without altering that of CD68 hyper-ramified cells in the FPC
entries.anchor: Results / The effects of roscovitine on microglia activation and monocyte infiltration following SE

entries.proposition: Fig 1C (publisher JPEG): CD68 amoeboid cells per 10^4 square micrometres read about 32 (vehicle) and about 12 (roscovitine), a fall of about 62 percent, while the text reports about 38 percent; the two agree only if 38 percent is read as the remaining fraction. The Iba-1 area (Fig 1B) is raised after status epilepticus in both arms (about 2.8 and 2.4 fold of control).
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1C amoeboid ~32 (vehicle) vs ~12 (roscovitine) *; ramified ~12 vs ~14; Fig 1B Iba-1 ~2.8 vs ~2.4 fold, both * vs control

entries.proposition: Roscovitine is described as a non-selective CDK5 inhibitor that also acts on Cdc2, CDK2, CDK9 and protein kinase A; the study does not separate which target explains the microglial effect and uses no EEG or seizure endpoint.
entries.snippet: However, roscovitine also affects the activities of Cdc2, CDK2, CDK9 and protein kinase A
